source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Ask for a detailed narrative of the traumatic event while the flashback is occurring so the memory can be processed immediately.","B":"Speak calmly and use simple grounding cues that orient the client to the present situation and current surroundings.","C":"Leave the client alone until the episode ends because interaction generally prolongs trauma-related flashbacks.","D":"Challenge the accuracy of the traumatic memory during the flashback to help the client distinguish it from current reality."}}
source_row.rationale: The VA National Center for PTSD describes grounding as a strategy for intrusive thoughts and flashbacks that helps the person focus on the current situation rather than the traumatic event. Calm, simple present-focused orientation is appropriate; detailed trauma processing is not the immediate goal during an acute flashback.
source_row.source_detail: Grounding for intrusive thoughts/flashbacks: focus attention on the current situation and present sensory surroundings.
